Alright, I've been iterating on the visual style of the forest scene. I added a canopy shade attribute, tweaked the instance counts, increased the number of blobs, adjusted their distribution, and even changed the number of cards per tree to make the foliage denser. Those changes were all aimed at improving the overall look and making the environment feel richer and more natural.

Now that those structural and procedural tweaks are in place, I need to address the final polish: the color of the tree trunks. Right now the trunk material is defined as:

```js
const trunkMat = new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ map: barkTex, roughness: 0.95, color: 0xb8a890 });
```

The hex value `0xb8a890` is a fairly muted, slightly brownish tone. Given the other adjustments—especially the brighter canopy shading and the increased foliage density—the trunks are looking a bit too dark and may be getting lost against the more vibrant background. I want the trunks to stand out a bit more and harmonize with the lighter, more saturated colors I've introduced elsewhere.

A simple way to achieve this is to shift the trunk color to a lighter, more desaturated shade. Picking a color like `0xd8c8b0` will give the trunks a softer, warmer appearance that complements the foliage without being overpowering. This change should make the trees feel more cohesive with the rest of the scene and improve overall visual balance.

Since this is just a single line change, I can use an Edit tool call targeting the exact line that defines `trunkMat`. I’ll replace the old color hex with the new one, keeping the rest of the material parameters unchanged.

Proceeding with the edit now.
